text: I understand the history of feeding difficulties and abdominal distension in this 8-month-old boy. To narrow down the differential, does the infant exhibit episodes of severe, colicky abdominal pain accompanied by drawing up of the legs or vomiting?

speaker: Doctor
text: Has there been any vomiting, and have you noticed any red or bloody "currant jelly" stools? I need to determine if there is bowel obstruction or ischemia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound is normal, I need to rule out metabolic causes for the feeding difficulties and distension. Has the baby had any episodes of unexplained lethargy, seizures, or a sweet/musty odor to his urine or sweat?

text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The worsening distension and failure to pass stool despite a normal ultrasound are highly concerning for a mechanical obstruction like intussusception that may have reduced or a distal blockage. I will proceed with the most likely diagnosis given the clinical deterioration.
